evidence: src/application/order-service.ts: OrderService is built only from OrderRepository and ProductRepository (constructor injection) and uses them for every read and write.
src/application/order-service.ts: requiredProduct and requiredOrder each hold their not-found rule in one place, and every public method reuses them.

src/application/order-service.ts: toProductView and toOrderView are the only places that map entities to views; addProduct, placeOrder, changeState, cancelOrder, listOrders and listProducts all go through them.
src/application/order-service.ts: state changes are left to the domain via order.advanceTo(state), order.cancel(), products[index].reserve(...) and product.release(...).
src/application/order-service.ts: ensureStockIsAvailable ignores its `products` parameter (`void products;`) and calls requiredProduct again. This is a redundant fetch, not a split in concerns.

src/application/order-service.ts: ensureStockIsAvailable checks `product.stock < quantity` after adding up quantities across lines. Product.reserve may also enforce stock limits, but product.ts is not provided, so the duplication is unconfirmed.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The unit is one file, src/application/order-service.ts, and it covers one concern: coordinating the fulfilment use cases. It handles adding and listing products and placing, advancing, cancelling and listing orders. It always works through the injected domain abstractions (OrderRepository and ProductRepository) and the domain entities' behaviour (Order.advanceTo, Order.cancel, Product.reserve, Product.release). It never touches persistence or state directly. The lookup-or-throw logic sits once in requiredProduct and requiredOrder, and the mapping to views sits once in toProductView and toOrderView. The private helpers use these consistently.

Smells (not failures):
1. ensureStockIsAvailable takes a `products` parameter, ignores it (`void products;`) and fetches each product again through requiredProduct. The caller placeOrder has already loaded them, so the repository is queried twice.
2. ensureStockIsAvailable checks `product.stock < quantity` itself, while Product.reserve may enforce the same rule. Product.ts is not in the material, so this duplication cannot be confirmed. The pre-check also adds up quantities across lines before any reservation, so no product is changed if one fails. That is a reasonable application-level job.

None of this splits the module into unrelated concerns or clearly bypasses its abstractions, so the unit passes, with moderate confidence.
